title: Engineering Trade-Off Database — Overview and definition
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Competing designs compared by cost, performance, reliability, energy, and complexity. The Engineering Trade-Off Database makes design decisions explicit: competing options laid side by side on cost, performance, reliability, energy, and complexity, with the weights stated and the winner justified — or the decision recorded as judgment call when numbers tie. Engineering is the art of compromise under constraints; this database turns 'we chose X' into a checkable record of why X beat Y.

title: Engineering Trade-Off Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Trade-study method: OPTIONS (2+ real alternatives, including 'do nothing' where relevant) -> CRITERIA (cost, performance, reliability, energy, complexity, schedule, risk — defined measurably) -> WEIGHTS (stated, summing to 1, with rationale) -> SCORES (per option per criterion, measured or estimated-with-basis) -> RANK (weighted sum) -> SENSITIVITY (vary weights +/- 20%, does the winner hold?) -> DECIDE (record + dissent + revisit triggers). Scoring honesty: measured scores cite the measurement; estimated scores cite the basis and carry uncertainty. Common traps: criteria that favor the pet option, weights tuned to justify a pre-made decision (sensitivity analysis exposes), ignoring the status quo option, deciding on total cost while ignoring schedule risk. Dissent is recorded — unanimous-by-silence is not consensus.

title: Engineering Trade-Off Database — Verification: tests and limitations
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Tests: scoring test (weighted sums verified); sensitivity test (stability computed correctly); completeness test (dissent and triggers present); determinism test. Limitations: scores are only as good as their basis; weights are judgment; real decisions need stakeholder review. Every study states measured vs estimated scores.

demo.title: Verification: trade-off scoring and sensitivity
demo.code: const opts={A:{perf:9,rel:6,simple:5},B:{perf:6,rel:9,simple:8}};const w={perf:0.5,rel:0.3,simple:0.2};function score(o){return o.perf*w.perf+o.rel*w.rel+o.simple*w.simple;}const sA=score(opts.A),sB=score(opts.B);const w2={perf:0.3,rel:0.5,simple:0.2};function score2(o){return o.perf*w2.perf+o.rel*w2.rel+o.simple*w2.simple;}const flip=score2(opts.B)>score2(opts.A);J({sA:+sA.toFixed(2),sB:+sB.toFixed(2),flip});assert(sA>sB&&flip,'tradeoff');
